prompt:
I need a PR description for a change I'm about to open on the Northwind orders service. The reviewer is Priya, who owns the database and has to approve anything touching the schema before it merges. Facts:
- Adds a composite index on orders(customer_id, created_at) in Postgres.
- The customer order history endpoint currently does a sequential scan. p95 latency is around 1.8 seconds for the largest tenants.
- On a staging copy of production data (about 42 million rows), the same query dropped to roughly 35 ms with the index.
- The migration uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, so there's no table lock. It took 11 minutes on staging, and production is about 1.4x bigger.
- The index adds about 2.1 GB of disk.
- I have not measured the effect on insert throughput. Orders peak around 900 writes per second during sales events, and I don't know if the extra index matters at that rate.
- Rollback is dropping the index. No code depends on it yet.
- We'd like to run it Tuesday night after the 22:00 traffic dip.
Write the description so I can paste it straight into the PR.

Can you write my weekly status update to Dana Okafor, our director of product? She reads these on Friday afternoon and uses them to decide what to escalate at Monday's leadership meeting. Here are this week's raw notes, sorry they're messy: The billing portal redesign shipped to 100% on Wednesday with no issues, and support tickets about invoices went from 61 to 38 week over week. Mobile offline mode is fine and on track for November 20. The Acme partner integration is the problem. Launch is planned for October 30, but Acme's sandbox has been down since Monday and we've lost four days of testing. Their contact says it'll be back 'early next week' but gave no firm date. If it's not back by Wednesday, we can't finish certification in time. The options are to slip the launch to November 13, or to launch on the 30th with only the read-only sync and ship write-back later. Sales promised write-back to two customers. I'm not sure which two, but Ravi in sales would know. I need Dana to pick one of the two options by Tuesday so I can tell Acme and sales. Also on hiring: one backend offer was accepted, and they start November 3.

I need to send an incident summary to the admin contacts at all our customers about yesterday's outage of Lumen, our scheduling product. These are IT admins and office managers, and most aren't engineers. They need to know what happened, whether their data is affected, and whether they need to do anything. Facts:
- The outage ran from 09:12 to 13:20 Eastern on October 15, so about four hours. Users couldn't log in or load calendars.
- Cause: an expired TLS certificate on an internal service that handles authentication. The renewal job had been failing silently since September.
- No data was lost. Bookings made through the public booking page during the window were queued and processed after recovery. We are still checking whether about 300 of them sent duplicate confirmation emails.
- Customers on SSO may need to sign in again. Everyone else doesn't need to do anything.
- We've added alerting on certificate expiry and are auditing all other certificates this week.
- Customers on the Business plan are eligible for an SLA credit. We haven't decided yet whether to apply it automatically or make them request it.
Please write the email.

Help me reply to Marcus Lee, our head of customer success. He emailed asking us to build bulk user import from CSV this quarter, because three enterprise customers asked for it during renewals. He wants a yes so he can tell them. It won't make this quarter. Facts:
- Our Q4 roadmap is committed to the SOC 2 audit work and the new permissions model, and bulk import depends on the permissions model.
- Permissions is due December 12. Bulk import could start after that, realistically in late January. That isn't committed until we finish Q1 planning on January 8.
- Engineering estimated import at about three weeks for one engineer.
- In the meantime, our support team can run imports manually from a spreadsheet, which takes them roughly an hour per customer. I haven't confirmed that support has capacity for three of these.
- I don't know the renewal dates for the three customers, but Marcus does.
Marcus needs to know what he can tell the customers. Write the reply.

I need to email Sofia at Brightline Hosting about our September invoice, number BL-20931. She's our account manager. One line looks wrong, and I want either a credit or an explanation before our finance team pays the invoice on October 31. Details: The invoice has a line 'Additional bandwidth overage: $4,860', which bills 54 TB of overage beyond our committed 20 TB at their rate of $90 per TB. Our own monitoring shows we used about 23 TB in total in September, so at most 3 TB over. That would be roughly $270. I'm not sure whether they count inbound traffic too, which our dashboard doesn't show. That could explain part of it, but probably not a 51 TB difference. We also had a DDoS attack on September 18 that they mitigated, and I don't know if that traffic got billed. The rest of the invoice looks fine and we're happy to pay that part now. Write the email.

I wrote this comment on the design doc for the new notification service, and it's not landing. The readers are the five engineers on the platform team plus Wen, the tech lead, who makes the final call. They need to pick approach A or B by Thursday's sync so Kofi can start building. Can you fix it and give me the final version?

Draft:
'Hey all, thanks for the great discussion so far, really appreciate everyone's input on this. I've been thinking a lot about the queueing question and I think there are some tradeoffs worth considering. Option A, using our existing Postgres with a jobs table, is nice because we already run it, though it might get slow at some point, hard to say. Option B, adding a managed queue like Kestrel MQ, is more scalable but obviously more stuff to run and it costs something, maybe a few hundred a month? Personally I lean a bit toward B but could go either way honestly. Anyway, it would be good to figure this out at some point soon. Let me know your thoughts!'

This is a draft announcement email to customers about a change to CSV exports in Ledgerly, our accounting app. It goes to every account owner. Many of them have spreadsheets or scripts that read our exports, and they need to know whether to update them before the change. Our marketing tool produced this and I don't like it. Please fix it and send back the final version.

Draft:
'Exciting news! At Ledgerly we're always working hard to make your experience better, and we're thrilled to share some amazing improvements to our export feature. Our team has been listening to your feedback and we've reimagined exports from the ground up to be more powerful and flexible than ever. Starting soon, exports will use a new and improved format with dates in ISO format, amounts without currency symbols, and a new column for tax category added after the amount column. The old format will be retired on November 30. If you have any integrations, you may want to take a look. As always, we're here to help!'

Where it says 'starting soon', the actual date is November 9, when the new format becomes the default.

My manager Elena can approve tooling spend under $15,000 herself. Anything above that she has to take to finance. I sent her this request and she replied 'what am I approving exactly?', so it clearly needs work. Please rewrite it and give me the final version.

Draft:
'Hi Elena, hope your week's going well! As you know the team has been struggling a bit with flaky tests and it's been really frustrating for everyone. I've been looking into some options and there's a tool called Sentinel CI that a lot of companies seem to like. It does test analytics and quarantining and a bunch of other stuff. It would probably save us a lot of time. Pricing is per seat, it's $40 per seat per month and we have 22 engineers, though maybe not everyone needs a seat. Last month we had about 140 reruns of failed builds, which is a lot. I think it's worth it. Would love to get your thoughts when you have a moment. Thanks!'

She needs to approve or reject it by the end of the month, when our free trial ends.

I'm kicking off our data retention project and drafted this note to the group, which includes people from legal, platform, the mobile team and support. Each owner needs to know what they own and by when, and everyone needs to confirm by Friday that the dates work. Please fix it and send back the final version.

Draft:
'Hi everyone! Super excited to kick off Project Tidewater, our big push on data retention. This is a really important initiative for the company and I know it'll be a great collaboration. As discussed, legal (Hannah) will figure out the retention periods, hopefully by early November, and then platform will build the deletion jobs, Tomás is leading that, aiming for mid-December. Mobile also needs to stop caching some stuff locally, Aisha I think you said you could take that, no rush but before January would be good. Support will need new macros at some point, not sure who yet. Our deadline from the regulator is January 31. Let's sync soon!'

Below is the executive summary from our postmortem on last week's payments delay. It goes to the leadership team, including the CEO and CFO, who will decide whether to fund the reliability work we're proposing for next quarter. A few of them will read only this paragraph. Please fix it and send back the final version.

Draft:
'On the evening of October 7, the team became aware of some issues affecting the payments pipeline. After extensive investigation involving multiple teams working tirelessly through the night, it was determined that a configuration change to the retry logic in the settlement worker had caused a backlog to form. Approximately 18,000 merchant payouts were delayed, some by up to 26 hours. The team rolled back the change and the backlog cleared by the following evening. There were a number of learnings. We are proposing an investment in staged config rollouts, which would require two engineers for one quarter. We are still confirming whether any merchants incurred late fees from their own banks as a result.'
